comparisons.peer_topic: Impact of cloud computing and hyperscaler power on competition
comparisons.peer_summary: The shift of data center workloads to the public cloud has increased the purchasing power of hyperscalers, heightened competitive pressures, and eroded Intel's competitive position due to demands for customization, performance, and efficiency.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and INTC disclose risks related to the shift of data center workloads to public cloud providers impacting their respective business models. AVGO warns that if customers shift compute workloads off-premises to public cloud providers, it could limit the market for its on-premises data center virtualization products. Similarly, INTC highlights that the increasing shift of data center workloads to the public cloud has increased the significance and purchasing power of hyperscalers, heightening competitive pressures. However, AVGO focuses on the demand risk for its specific software/virtualization portfolio, whereas INTC focuses on the erosion of its competitive position due to the demands of cloud environments and hyperscaler influence.

sentences.text: If businesses build new or shift existing compute workloads off-premises to public cloud providers, this could limit the market for on-premises deployments of our data center virtualization products.

Industry trends, such as the increasing shift of data center workloads to the public cloud, have increased the significance and purchasing power of certain customers, particularly hyperscalers, in some of our data center-focused businesses.

The further consolidation of computing workloads in the cloud, and consolidation among cloud service providers, can heighten the competitive importance of factors such as collaboration and customization with cloud service provider customers to optimize products for their environments; optimization for cloud services and applications; product performance; energy efficiency; feature differentiation; product quality, reliability, and factors affecting server uptime; and product security and security features.

comparisons.peer_summary: Cloud service providers are developing their own semiconductors and abstracting hardware through software, making it difficult to differentiate Intel's products and potentially reducing demand for Intel chips.
comparisons.comparison: INTC discloses that the shift of data center workloads to the cloud has adversely affected sales to enterprise customers who migrate workloads from internal infrastructures to cloud service providers. This mirrors AVGO's risk that customers shifting workloads to public cloud providers will limit demand for AVGO's on-premises solutions. The common topic is the displacement of on-premises/internal infrastructure demand by cloud migration, though INTC also notes the resulting difficulty in differentiating products due to software abstraction.

sentences.text: If businesses build new or shift existing compute workloads off-premises to public cloud providers, this could limit the market for on-premises deployments of our data center virtualization products.

The shift of data center workloads to the cloud has also adversely affected, and may continue to affect, sales to enterprise customers when end users have elected to migrate workloads from their own internal data center infrastructures to cloud service providers.

comparisons.peer_topic: Requirements for success in adapting to industry changes
comparisons.peer_summary: Success depends on timely adaptation to industry changes, R&D investments, launching new business models like cloud solutions, expanding ecosystems, managing lifecycles, securing infrastructure, and making necessary investments.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and NVDA identify the launch of new business models, including cloud solutions, as a critical dependency for success. AVGO notes its software products are based on hybrid-cloud technologies and that customer acceptance of these strategies is vital. NVDA explicitly lists launching new offerings with new business models including software, services, and cloud solutions as a requirement for its success. While AVGO frames this as a risk if acceptance fails, NVDA frames it as a necessary strategic action to meet evolving market needs.
